title: Care and an outcome
hook: An example can suggest a question without settling it.

knows: Animals can act and respond to conditions.
doesNotKnow: In a toy observation, 4 of 6 young survive with one caregiver and 5 of 6 with two. What can this single record establish?

misconception: One observed behavior always supports a broad or causal conclusion.
objective: In a toy observation, 4 of 6 young survive with one caregiver and 5 of 6 with two. What can this single record establish?

claims.text: In a toy observation, 4 of 6 young survive with one caregiver and 5 of 6 with two. What can this single record establish? The stipulated outcomes are 4 of 6 and 5 of 6, a difference of one young in this example. Other conditions could differ, and chance can matter. One observation does not establish that the number of caregivers caused the difference or that the outcome always holds.
claims.source: Stipulated toy observations; not observed animal data. Source lead, not checked: OpenStax Biology 2e, Behavioral Biology, https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/45-7-behavioral-biology

claims.text: The panels show a stipulated illustrative scenario, not observations or measurements of real animals.
Two toy groups have 3 and 4 surviving young. Does that single record alone establish why the outcomes differ? A difference in one record alone does not identify its cause.

options: Yes, it proves the result always holds
